items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Another act was the Will Mast/en trio of whom the youngest in the act was Sammy Davis Jr. ... Sammy used to call me BeBop, but I certainly wasn't playing that style.

ctx.x: From Cincinnati, we went to Dayton for one night and then to Detroit for a one week engagement at the Paradise theatre. The pit band who played one number before the show and one after, was lead by Buddy Bowen, a sax alto man, whom I had met in New York when he played for a while at the Savoy with another orchestra that I don'tt remember the name. Buddy was also the walking delegate for the musicians union and the trumpet player was Georges(Buddy)Lee, whom I had played with in Wes Helvey's orchestra in…

Another act was the Will Mast/en trio of whom the youngest in the act was Sammy Davis Jr. Sammy was unknown at that time, but he was responsible for the success of the trio, because he was a fine singer and tap dancer. His uncle Will Mast/en, and his father, Sammy Davis Senior, were the members of the trio. Sammy used to call me BeBop, but I certainly wasn't playing that style.

After the week in Detroit, Sy hired a bus to take us to Gary, Indiana, for a one night stand. Before we arrived in Gary, the windshield of the bus blew out. I never knew the reason it happened, but there it was, all shattered to hell, but we made it to the gig. Then the bus driver went over to Chicago whichis not far from Gary and had a new windshield put in and returned to Gary 1 a.m We were leaving that morning for Indianapolis after the dance.
